original_test_intent: Verify every installed and in-scope NIC exposed by Linux has the expected PCI identity, interface/MAC mapping, driver and firmware version.
original_method: On the approved host, securely enumerate complete PCI/network/sysfs data, map every relevant interface to PCI BDF and driver, collect per-interface ethtool firmware evidence, preserve raw output/checksums and compare with the signed NIC matrix.
manual_activity: User supplies the approved per-NIC matrix and interface-scope policy; agent can perform complete read-only collection.
required_inputs: Approved Linux host identity and secure access
Expected NIC vendor/device/subsystem, PCI slot/BDF or topology, MAC, driver and firmware matrix
Policy for embedded, BMC, virtual, bond/VLAN and InfiniBand interfaces
pciutils, iproute2, ethtool and sysfs permissions
Protected evidence and hardware-identifier privacy policy
safety_requirements: Verify exact host and management-path interface before reads
Use managed authentication/host verification and least privilege
Protect MAC/topology identifiers and preserve complete raw evidence
Stop on wrong host, missing mapping, privilege failure, contradictory identity or driver error
No link state, address, driver, firmware or network configuration change
agent_execution_scope: Enumerate every relevant PCI NIC and interface, map MAC/driver/firmware and capture checksums/status
Report explicit unavailable/unsupported fields and compare to supplied matrix
Do not stop after first interface, toggle links, reload drivers, update firmware or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Provide authoritative per-NIC expected matrix and interface scope
Resolve SR-IOV/PF/VF, virtual, BMC or driver-specific mapping gaps

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Directionally correct but incomplete/unsafe: filtering, truncation and `break` omit adapters and evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Securely collect complete `lspci -nnvv`, `ip -details link`, sysfs PCI/interface mapping and `ethtool -i` for every approved interface with raw checksums/status.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NIC identity, MAC, firmware and5/5 fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a one-to-one table from physical/PCI identity through netdev/MAC to driver and firmware, retaining all interfaces and unsupported-query results.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exhaustive coverage, topology binding, secure access and immutable evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The first-interface-only prior command cannot satisfy a multi-NIC platform and is rejected.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Interface names are not stable identities, ethtool firmware fields are driver-dependent, and virtual or management interfaces may lack direct PCI mappings.

project_override_considerations: Project must explicitly include/exclude BMC-shared, dedicated management, virtual, bond/VLAN, PF/VF and InfiniBand devices; no interface is silently ignored.
expected_evidence: Complete lspci identity/link data for all in-scope NICs
All interface names/MACs/states/addresses and sysfs PCI/driver mapping
Per-interface driver/module/version and firmware fields or explicit unsupported results
Expected-versus-observed NIC matrix, raw checksums and command status
dmesg/syslog/SEL/network errors and final unchanged link/configuration state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: NIC information, MAC and firmware criteria are internally consistent. Exact device matrix and interface scope are project readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Host, tools, permissions and expected matrix can be supplied; the read-only inventory is automatable.

review_improvement: Eliminates the first-interface coverage hole and binds every MAC/driver/firmware result to an unambiguous PCI device.
independent_technical_reasoning: A server can expose multiple onboard, add-in, management, InfiniBand and virtual functions. Interface order and names are not reliable device identity, and firmware queried from only the first netdev can falsely represent the entire system. Each expected physical/function identity must be joined through sysfs to its netdev and MAC before per-device firmware comparison is complete.
